questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Bucket has red rose’ is written as ‘Tu Ea Oic Li’; ‘Home’s rose white colour’ is written as ‘Qhi Sa Uic Ea’; ‘Fresh colour red there’ is written as ‘Uic Hi Li No’; and ‘There demand white bucket’ is written as ‘Ao Oic Qhi Hi’. What is the code for ‘Has’? / ‘Has’ के लिए कूट क्या है?
questions.explanation: Compare ‘Bucket has red rose’ with ‘Home’s rose white colour’: their only common word is rose and their only common code is Ea, so rose = Ea. The remaining three codes in the first sentence are Tu, Oic, and Li for bucket, has, and red. ‘There demand white bucket’ shares bucket with the first sentence, and the common code is Oic, so bucket = Oic. Comparing the first and third sentences identifies red = Li. The remaining code for has is Tu.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 4; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Bucket has red rose’ is written as ‘Tu Ea Oic Li’; ‘Home’s rose white colour’ is written as ‘Qhi Sa Uic Ea’; ‘Fresh colour red there’ is written as ‘Uic Hi Li No’; and ‘There demand white bucket’ is written as ‘Ao Oic Qhi Hi’. What is the code for ‘Home’s there red’, respectively?
questions.explanation: The common word/code comparisons give Home’s = Sa. ‘There’ is the common word between ‘Fresh colour red there’ and ‘There demand white bucket’; their common code is Hi. ‘Red’ is identified as Li by comparing the first and third statements after matching the other shared terms. Thus Home’s, there, and red are coded Sa, Hi, and Li, respectively.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 6; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Bucket has red rose’ is written as ‘Tu Ea Oic Li’; ‘Home’s rose white colour’ is written as ‘Qhi Sa Uic Ea’; ‘Fresh colour red there’ is written as ‘Uic Hi Li No’; and ‘There demand white bucket’ is written as ‘Ao Oic Qhi Hi’. What does ‘No’ represent?
questions.explanation: In the first and third statements, the common words are red and colour, and the common codes are Li and Uic. Red is Li, so colour is Uic. The remaining code No in the third statement therefore represents Fresh.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 7; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Bucket has red rose’ is written as ‘Tu Ea Oic Li’; ‘Home’s rose white colour’ is written as ‘Qhi Sa Uic Ea’; ‘Fresh colour red there’ is written as ‘Uic Hi Li No’; and ‘There demand white bucket’ is written as ‘Ao Oic Qhi Hi’. What does ‘Ea Qhi Oic’ represent?
questions.explanation: The statements establish Ea = rose, Qhi = white, and Oic = bucket. Therefore ‘Ea Qhi Oic’ represents ‘rose white bucket’, which is the same set of words as option D, ‘White rose bucket’.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 8; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Bucket has red rose’ is written as ‘Tu Ea Oic Li’; ‘Home’s rose white colour’ is written as ‘Qhi Sa Uic Ea’; ‘Fresh colour red there’ is written as ‘Uic Hi Li No’; and ‘There demand white bucket’ is written as ‘Ao Oic Qhi Hi’. What is a possible code for ‘he has fresh demand’?
questions.explanation: The statements establish has = Tu, fresh = No, and demand = Ao. The word ‘he’ does not appear in the coding statements, so its code is not fixed. Option A contains the three required codes and one otherwise unspecified code Pa, making it a possible code.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 9; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Today he feels good’ is written as ‘Zi Li Ki Ti’; ‘His work completed today’ is written as ‘Di Ki Si Fi’; ‘Feels his mind good’ is written as ‘Si Zi Ti Bi’; and ‘Good energy takes time’ is written as ‘Gi Xi Vi Zi’. If ‘Today takes his’ is coded as ‘Gi Si Ki’, what is the code for ‘Energy’?
questions.explanation: The added phrase confirms takes = Gi, while the shared statements identify today = Ki and his = Si. In ‘Good energy takes time’ (Gi Xi Vi Zi), Gi is takes and Zi is good, leaving Xi and Vi for energy and time. The supplied information does not distinguish which is energy, so the answer cannot be determined.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 11; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Today he feels good’ is written as ‘Zi Li Ki Ti’; ‘His work completed today’ is written as ‘Di Ki Si Fi’; ‘Feels his mind good’ is written as ‘Si Zi Ti Bi’; and ‘Good energy takes time’ is written as ‘Gi Xi Vi Zi’. What is the code for ‘Work’?
questions.explanation: The common words in the first and second statements show today = Ki; the first and third show his = Si. In ‘His work completed today’ (Di Ki Si Fi), removing the known codes for his and today leaves Di and Fi for work and completed. The source provides no way to distinguish those two words, so either code is possible for Work.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 12; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Today he feels good’ is written as ‘Zi Li Ki Ti’; ‘His work completed today’ is written as ‘Di Ki Si Fi’; ‘Feels his mind good’ is written as ‘Si Zi Ti Bi’; and ‘Good energy takes time’ is written as ‘Gi Xi Vi Zi’. What word does the code ‘Si’ represent?
questions.explanation: The second and third statements share ‘His’ and ‘work completed today’ does not share the code Si with the first. More directly, the overlap between ‘His work completed today’ and ‘Feels his mind good’ includes the unique common code Si for the common word His. Thus Si represents His.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 13; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘Today he feels good’ is written as ‘Zi Li Ki Ti’; ‘His work completed today’ is written as ‘Di Ki Si Fi’; ‘Feels his mind good’ is written as ‘Si Zi Ti Bi’; and ‘Good energy takes time’ is written as ‘Gi Xi Vi Zi’. If ‘His market mind’ is written as ‘Bi Si Ci’, what is the code for ‘Market’?
questions.explanation: The earlier statements identify His = Si. In the added phrase, the remaining words market and mind correspond to Bi and Ci, but the source gives no information that distinguishes them. Market may therefore be coded Bi or Ci, matching option D.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 01_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 1, PDF page 14; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain language: ‘King proposed strict rule’ is coded as ‘su da nic ki’; ‘Weak rule corrupt system’ is coded as ‘phi ra tic da’; ‘Good system strict desire’ is coded as ‘tic gi ki mo’; and ‘Desire change corrupt king’ is coded as ‘zo nic phi gi’. What is the code for ‘proposed good rule queen’?
questions.explanation: The statements establish proposed = su, rule = da, good = mo, and system = tic. However, ‘queen’ does not occur in any coding statement, so its code is unknown and the complete four-word code cannot be determined from the passage. The source’s option ‘NOT’ is the only option expressing that the proposed code is unsupported.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 4; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘Global Warming Climate Change’ means ‘ig ph vm at’; ‘Climate Weather Emissions Mitigation’ means ‘ph vs ys pr’; ‘Change Greenhouse Gas Weather’ means ‘ig le zx vs’; and ‘Warming Greenhouse Fossil fuel’ means ‘vm le im hl’. What is the code for ‘Greenhouse’?
questions.explanation: Greenhouse appears in the third and fourth coded statements. Their only common word is Greenhouse and their only common code is le, so Greenhouse = le.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 5; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘Global Warming Climate Change’ means ‘ig ph vm at’; ‘Climate Weather Emissions Mitigation’ means ‘ph vs ys pr’; ‘Change Greenhouse Gas Weather’ means ‘ig le zx vs’; and ‘Warming Greenhouse Fossil fuel’ means ‘vm le im hl’. What does ‘im’ represent?
questions.explanation: In ‘Warming Greenhouse Fossil fuel’ coded ‘vm le im hl’, the other statements identify Warming = vm and Greenhouse = le. The remaining codes im and hl therefore correspond to Fossil and fuel in either order. Thus im may represent Fossil or fuel (option E).
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 6; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘Global Warming Climate Change’ means ‘ig ph vm at’; ‘Climate Weather Emissions Mitigation’ means ‘ph vs ys pr’; ‘Change Greenhouse Gas Weather’ means ‘ig le zx vs’; and ‘Warming Greenhouse Fossil fuel’ means ‘vm le im hl’. What is a possible code for ‘Warming Gas’?
questions.explanation: Warming occurs in the first and fourth statements; their only shared code is vm, so Warming = vm. Greenhouse = le from the third and fourth statements; therefore in the third statement Gas can be zx (the other remaining code after Change = ig and Weather = vs). The pair vm zx is consequently a possible code for Warming Gas.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 7; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘enters before missile war’ is coded as ‘im qk yi oj’; ‘attack sky missile on’ is coded as ‘my xm ex yi’; ‘people attack not enters’ is coded as ‘go oj ex mf’; and ‘before attack safe on’ is coded as ‘jx my ex qk’. Which option gives the code for ‘sky’? / दी गई कूट भाषा में ‘sky’ के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कूट है?
questions.explanation: ‘Attack’ appears in statements 2, 3, and 4; ex is the common code across the statements, so attack = ex. In statements 2 and 4, attack and on are shared; after removing ex, my is on. Missile is shared by statements 1 and 2 and has code yi. In statement 2, the remaining code for sky is xm.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 8; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘enters before missile war’ is coded as ‘im qk yi oj’; ‘attack sky missile on’ is coded as ‘my xm ex yi’; ‘people attack not enters’ is coded as ‘go oj ex mf’; and ‘before attack safe on’ is coded as ‘jx my ex qk’. If ‘safe people always’ is written as ‘xw jx mf’, what is the code for ‘always sky before’? / यदि ‘safe people always’ को ‘xw jx mf’ के रूप में लिखा जाता है, तो ‘always sky before’ का कूट क्या होगा?
questions.explanation: From the coded statements, before = qk, sky = xm, and safe = jx. In the added phrase ‘safe people always’ = ‘xw jx mf’, safe accounts for jx; the page’s worked annotations pair people with mf, leaving always = xw. The required codes are therefore xw, xm, and qk; option C contains those three codes.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 10; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘enters before missile war’ is coded as ‘im qk yi oj’; ‘attack sky missile on’ is coded as ‘my xm ex yi’; ‘people attack not enters’ is coded as ‘go oj ex mf’; and ‘before attack safe on’ is coded as ‘jx my ex qk’. What does the code ‘go’ stand for? / दी गई कूट भाषा में कोड ‘go’ का क्या अर्थ है?
questions.explanation: The third statement contains people, attack, not, and enters with codes go, oj, ex, and mf. The other statements establish attack = ex and enters = oj. The remaining two words people/not can correspond to go/mf in either order, so go cannot be identified uniquely.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 12; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘enters before missile war’ is coded as ‘im qk yi oj’; ‘attack sky missile on’ is coded as ‘my xm ex yi’; ‘people attack not enters’ is coded as ‘go oj ex mf’; and ‘before attack safe on’ is coded as ‘jx my ex qk’. Which option gives the code for ‘war’? / दी गई कूट भाषा में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कूट ‘war’ के लिए है?
questions.explanation: The statements identify enters = oj (from the first and third), missile = yi (from the first and second), and before = qk (from the first and fourth). In the first statement, the remaining code im corresponds to war.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 14; topic: Chinese coding

questions.question_text: In a certain code language: ‘enters before missile war’ is coded as ‘im qk yi oj’; ‘attack sky missile on’ is coded as ‘my xm ex yi’; ‘people attack not enters’ is coded as ‘go oj ex mf’; and ‘before attack safe on’ is coded as ‘jx my ex qk’. Which option may be the code for ‘people safe’? / दी गई कूट भाषा में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कूट ‘people safe’ के लिए हो सकता है?
questions.explanation: Safe occurs only in the fourth statement, where its possible codes are the codes left after identifying before = qk, attack = ex, and on = my; this leaves jx. In the third statement, after identifying attack = ex and enters = oj, people/not are go/mf in either order. Therefore jx mf is a possible code for people safe.
questions.source: Coding Decoding 02_Class Notes.pdf, lecture 2, PDF page 16; topic: Chinese coding
